html:
A hard red winter wheat brought to Kansas in 1874 by Mennonite settlers from the Russian Empire, which helped turn the Great Plains into one of the world's breadbaskets.

The Russian Mennonites were Protestant farmers of Dutch and North German origin who had farmed the steppes of Ukraine for a century. When Russia began ending their exemption from military service, thousands moved to the American and Canadian prairies, recruited by railways such as the Santa Fe that wanted settlers. They brought seed of a wheat suited to the steppe.

Winter wheat is sown in autumn and harvested in early summer. Turkey Red stood up to the cold winters and dry summers of the plains far better than the soft wheats other settlers tried. New mills learned to grind its hard grain into fine flour. By the early 1900s it covered most of the wheat fields of Kansas and nearby states. It made the plains a great exporter of grain, and fed the wheat boom that later ended in the Dust Bowl.
sum: A hard red winter wheat brought to Kansas in 1874 by Mennonite settlers from the Russian Empire, which helped turn the Great Plains into one of the world's breadbaskets.
